claims.text: The investigated alloy is AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The initial HEA is in the as-cast condition.
The HEA has a fine lamellar dual-phase L12/B2 microstructure.
The microstructure contains approximately 71% L12 and 29% B2.
The coupled tribo-corrosion response is governed by the HEA's ability to maintain robust, homogeneous Cr-dependent passivation.
Robust Cr-dependent passivation facilitates rapid repassivation.
Robust Cr-dependent passivation promotes formation of a stable, low-shear tribo-layer.
The stable, low-shear tribo-layer minimizes both mechanical wear and corrosion.
Retention of the fine L12/B2 lamellar structure supports a uniform Cr distribution.
Uniform Cr distribution enables efficient passive-film repair.
Uniform Cr distribution stabilizes the tribo-layer during sliding.
Temperature modulates the competition between sliding-induced depassivation and thermally activated repassivation.
At approximately 50 °C, rapid film repair supports a stable, compacted, low-shear tribo-layer.
At 25 °C, slower repassivation favors two-body abrasive wear.
At 100 °C, intermittent passive-film rupture produces debris-driven oxidative wear.
The HEA will have a lower coefficient of friction than identically treated duplex stainless steel 2205 and than the HEA tested at 25 or 100 °C, particularly near 50 °C.
The HEA will have lower wear volume than identically treated duplex stainless steel 2205 and than the HEA tested at 25 or 100 °C, particularly near 50 °C.
The HEA will have a lower tribo-corrosion wear rate than identically treated duplex stainless steel 2205 and than the HEA tested at 25 or 100 °C, particularly near 50 °C.
The prediction is expected to hold in deionized water over 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, 3–9 Hz, and a 3.5 mm reciprocating stroke.
The mechanism may not apply during continuous high-temperature operation, long-term aging, or exposure to different ionic compositions.
